sections.text:
1 Haec de tempestatibus exilia praesagia ex longiore opere excerpta esse credi-
derim forsitan versibus concepto. Astrologus quem epitomator expilavit, non solum
de aeris mutationibus agebat sed de terrae motibus, quorum in titulo tantum
(σεισμῶν) fit mentio, et de multis aliis eventis, quod frustulum p. 86, 14 servatum
(καὶ στρατόπεδον - ἀνδρός) prodit. De auctore coniecturis abstinere praestat,
donec eiusdem tractatus alia recensio edatur plenior, ut videtur, quae in cod.
Flor. 12, f. 95-98 exstat (Inc. Περὶ τροπῆς ἀέρων ἐκ τῶν Χαλδαϊκῶν καὶ Αἰγυπτια-
κῶν ἐν ἐπιτομῇ ...). — Attamen cum vv. 42 ss. conferre iuvabit omina Iovis in
singulis zodiaci signis quae Zoroastro tribuuntur in Geoponicis, I, 12.
sections.en: 1 I would believe that these meager presages concerning weather have been excerpted from a longer work perhaps conceived in verses. The astrologer whom the epitomator pillaged was treating not only of changes of the air but of earthquakes, of which mention is made only in the title (σεισμῶν), and of many other events, which the fragment preserved on p. 86, 14 (καὶ στρατόπεδον - ἀνδρός) reveals. It is better to abstain from conjectures concerning the author, until another fuller recension of the same treatise is edited, as it seems, which exists in cod. Flor. 12, f. 95-98 (Inc. Περὶ τροπῆς ἀέρων ἐκ τῶν Χαλδαϊκῶν καὶ Αἰγυπτιακῶν ἐν ἐπιτομῇ ...). — Nevertheless it will be helpful to compare with vv. 42 ff. the omens of Jupiter in the individual signs of the zodiac which are attributed to Zoroaster in the Geoponica, I, 12.

summary.headline: Horoscope Methods and Weather Omens
summary.text: Discussion of accurately finding the horoscoping degree through the Sun’s epoch, trigon-based monomoiria, and Ptolemy’s tables, followed by section 52 on weather conditions and Saturn’s omens for rain, clouds, disease, winds, thunder, and lightning.
